test_title: PYST 38 - SSC CHSL 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 26 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Ravi invested Rs. 25,000 in two schemes for 3 years. Both schemes offer 12% p.a. interest. One gives simple interest and the other gives compound interest (compounded annually). Find the difference between the interests earned from both schemes.
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 25,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 12% p.a.

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Compound Interest (CI) = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T - P

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = (25,000 × 12 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = Rs. 9,000

⇒ CI = 25,000 × (1 + 12 ÷ 100)³ - 25,000

⇒ CI = 25,000 × (1.12)³ - 25,000

⇒ CI = 25,000 × 1.404928 - 25,000

⇒ CI = Rs. 35,123.2 - Rs. 25,000

⇒ CI = Rs. 10,123.2

⇒ Difference = CI - SI

⇒ Difference = Rs. 10,123.2 - Rs. 9,000

⇒ Difference = Rs. 1,123.2

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1123.2.**
